title: Peacemakers: Horrors of War - prototype preview
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mHE2XXExu7Q

Daniel (@dungeondive) previews a prototype of Peacemakers: Horrors of War from Sami Laakso, set in the same animal-folk world as Lands of Galzyr, one of his favourite games. It replaces Dawn of the Peacemakers, known to him only through Mike DiLisio's enthusiasm. In this co-op war game for one to four players, your adventurers try to stop a war instead of winning one. Each faction has a morale track, and you win when both sides end a round in the green zone together and sign a treaty. Break either side all the way to surrender and you lose.

Each turn you draw four multi-use resource cards. The top half surveys a faction's next order, moves you, fortifies a hex or delegates a card to a teammate. The bottom half is a special trick, such as food-poisoning the Scarlet Macaw commander, whose timid order only lowers morale while he's wounded. The factions run on two programmed decks: half-cards combine into initiative, morale changes and advances, so scenario mastery means learning each army's habits. Every casualty shuffles a Horrors of War card into your deck, so your peacekeepers are worn down by what they witness. Seeding them in raises the difficulty.

There are six scenarios, each with peace, no-casualty and two bespoke achievements. The factions include ocelots, spectacled bears, toucans and strawberry poison frogs with blowguns, all on standees he adores as a fan of Watership Down and Redwall. His one worry is four-player turns. It's on Gamefound.

----

Peacemakers asks you to end a war rather than win it. What other games have flipped a familiar genre's goal in a way that worked for you?
